scenes.title: The plan
scenes.vo: Here's the plan. First, the key ideas. Then, a worked example, step by step. Then, your checklist. And finally, a three-question quiz.
scenes.cap: Here's the plan. First, the key ideas. Then, a worked example, step by step. Then, your checklist. And finally, a three-question quiz.

scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: What you actually get equals quoted output minus price impact minus pool fees minus gas. First, AMM decks: you trade against a liquidity pool priced by a formula (Lesson 2.2). Next, On-chain order book: orders matched by price and time, fully or partly on-chain. Then, Aggregator: searches many pools and venues and may split your order across routes. Also, Price impact: how much your trade moves the price. It grows with size relative to pool depth. On top of that, Slippage tolerance: the worst price you'll accept before the transaction reverts.
scenes.cap: What you actually get = quoted output − price impact − pool fees − gas. First, AMM DEX: you trade against a liquidity pool priced by a formula (Lesson 2.2). Next, On-chain order book: orders matched by price and time, fully or partly on-chain. Then, Aggregator: searches many pools and venues and may split your order across routes. Also, Price impact: how much your trade moves the price. It grows with size relative to pool depth. On top of that, Slippage tolerance: the worst price you'll accept before the transaction reverts.

scenes.title: Key ideas (cont.)
scenes.vo: And finally, Routing: multi-hop routes (A to B to C) can give a better price but touch more contracts.
scenes.cap: And finally, Routing: multi-hop routes (A → B → C) can give a better price but touch more contracts.

scenes.title: Worked example
scenes.vo: Selling 20 ETH: The aggregator wins by about $308. Now selling 0.5 ETH: the aggregator quotes $3 better but costs $12 more in gas, so the direct pool wins. Big trades benefit from routing. Small trades mostly lose to gas. Single pool direct, 59,100 U.S.D.C., $8, 59,092. Aggregator (split across 3 pools), 59,420 U.S.D.C., $20, 59,400.

Route uses reputable pools and tokens you've verified

scenes.q: Why can an aggregator give a better price?
scenes.a: It can split an order across pools, so each pool's price moves less.
scenes.vo: Question one. Why can an aggregator give a better price? [[pause 4]] The answer: It can split an order across pools, so each pool's price moves less.

scenes.q: When does the best quote lose?
scenes.a: When the extra gas costs more than the price improvement, which is common for small trades.
